tf27b.title: Qwen3.8 27B
tf27b.tagline: The all-rounder: fast decode with DFlash2 drafts, images and video, eight requests at once.

install.time: 15–30 minutes: pulls or builds the TensorFold image and downloads ~19 GB of weights

perf.source: sparkDash (MiaAI-Lab), prose; code decodes at 136.9 tok/s

tf27b.eta: about a minute (the very first start compiles kernels: a few minutes)

tfflash.title: Qwen3.8 Flash Next
tfflash.tagline: The strongest model that fits one Spark: a 125B mixture of experts on NVIDIA's FP4 checkpoint, close to full precision. Reads images (video and PDFs optional), windows up to 1M, and an abliterated option.
tfflash.engine: TensorFold v1.2.7 Zig engine · NVIDIA FP4 (QAD) · MTP drafts

install.time: 1–2 hours: builds the engine image (no prebuilt image is published for v1.2.7 yet) and downloads the ~96 GiB checkpoint
install.note: Needs about 160 GB of free disk. The engine build needs at least 10 GiB of free memory: if a large model is serving and memory is tight, it stops and says so — switch to a smaller model first, then install.

perf.source: the recipe's own tools/bench_streams.py on the v1.2.7 build (greedy, 256 tokens, median of 3): 58.5 tok/s alone and 230.1 across 5 on prose, 51.9 and 206.8 on code; prefill 2,303–2,443 tok/s, a 200K-token prompt in 95.7 s

tfflash.eta: a few minutes (loads ~81 GiB of weights)
notes: 256K and 128K run the v1.2.7 build, which has no YaRN. 512K and 1M run the long-context build: the recipe's earlier TensorFold engine with the INT4-AutoRound checkpoint (about 10% lower general scores on its authors' harness), YaRN ×4, images and video, no abliterated or PDF. It is a separate ~160 GB install: Options… offers it. Apps keep the same model ID whichever window serves. Abliterated at 512K: use the Qwen3.8 Flash Next (vLLM) card with Abliterated on.
Images go in as image_url parts with data: URLs (JPEG or WebP, up to 50 a request); public https:// links are refused.

Installed before November 2026? Press Update recipe… below: it pulls the v1.2.7 recipe and builds its engine image (about an hour; the weights aren't downloaded again). Abliterated, video and PDF need it.

contexts.label: 256K
contexts.detail: the longest window this engine serves, five chats at once — no room for pictures

contexts.label: 128K
contexts.detail: two chats at once, and ~28 GiB kept free so Qwen-Image can draw beside it

contexts.label: 512K
contexts.detail: longer chats: YaRN ×4 on the long-context build (INT4 checkpoint, three full windows at once)

install.time: 1–2 hours: pulls or builds its engine image and downloads the ~122 GiB INT4 checkpoint

contexts.label: 1M
contexts.detail: the longest chats: YaRN ×4 on the long-context build (INT4 checkpoint, one full 1M window, shorter chats share the rest)

install.time: 1–2 hours: pulls or builds its engine image and downloads the ~122 GiB INT4 checkpoint

switches.name: ablit
switches.label: Abliterated
switches.detail: drowzeys's Keys house-qsa overlay: the 12 attention layers' output projections with the refusal direction projected out (a ~190 MB download, on the first start only). Everything else stays NVIDIA's checkpoint.
switches.warn: This model has had its safety refusals removed. The overlay is gated: accept its Responsible Use Agreement on Hugging Face (signed in) and save a token on the Settings tab first. The recipe has booted it, but hasn't run its accuracy or refusal checks on it yet.

switches.name: video
switches.label: Video input
switches.detail: video parts (MP4, MOV, WebM; 2 frames a second, counted against the 50-image budget — about 50 seconds a request). The recipe builds it but hasn't run a live video request yet.

switches.name: pdf
switches.label: PDF input
switches.detail: PDF document parts (OpenAI file / input_file, Anthropic document, or a data:application/pdf image_url), rendered to page images by the engine's PDFium: up to 32 MiB and 16 pages, sharing the image budget.

switches.name: thinking
switches.label: Thinking by default
switches.detail: the model reasons before it answers unless a request says otherwise (chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking). Off: quick answers by default.

bolt.title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt
bolt.tagline: NVIDIA's 74B reasoner packed into 23 GB: sixteen requests at once, images and video, and most of the Spark's memory left over.
bolt.engine: TensorFold Zig engine · IQ2_XXS + NVFP4 · LiLiCorr drafts

install.time: 20–60 minutes: downloads ~25 GB of weights and builds the engine image (no prebuilt image is published for the current revision)
install.note: The engine build needs at least 10 GiB of free memory and about 40 GB of free disk. If a large model is serving and memory is tight, switch to a smaller one first.

perf.source: the recipe's own measurement of 2026-10-20 (TensorFold's bench_concurrent.py, greedy, thinking off, 256 tokens): 73.7 tok/s alone on prose, 240.3 across 8; code 137.3 alone, 342 across 8

bolt.eta: about a minute (loads ~23 GiB of weights)

nemotron.title: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
nemotron.tagline: NVIDIA's quick reasoner: 30B MoE (3B active), 1M context, dozens of requests at once.

install.time: 10–20 minutes: downloads ~21 GB of weights and the SGLang image

perf.source: community measurement of the same model and DSpark drafter on a DGX Spark (vLLM, code; Classmethod) — this recipe serves it with SGLang

nemotron.eta: a few minutes (it checks for a newer image first)

laguna.title: Laguna S 2.1
laguna.tagline: Poolside's 118B coding model in 4-bit, with DFlash drafts: 256K context, tool calling and reasoning.

install.time: 1–2 hours: pulls the vLLM image and downloads ~100 GB of weights
install.note: Needs about 125 GB of free disk. Weights go to the Hugging Face cache, shared with the recipes.

perf.source: the recipe's own benchmark chart: 76.7 tok/s for one request, 34.9 each with 4 at once

laguna.eta: about 15 minutes the first time (kernel compilation); faster after
notes: The recipe's limit of 4 requests at once is deliberate: DFlash crashes at vLLM's default of 256.
The first start installs matching FlashInfer kernels from flashinfer.ai, so the box needs internet then.

inkling.title: Inkling 2 Mini
inkling.tagline: Thinking Machines' looped 26B MoE (3.4B active) in 20 GB: images in, reasoning, tool calling and 256K context, with most of the Spark left free.
inkling.engine: vLLM (Inkling build) · NVFP4 + MXFP8 · DSpark drafts

install.time: 20–40 minutes: pulls the ~11 GB vLLM image and downloads ~20 GB of weights
install.note: Needs about 35 GB of free disk. Weights go to the Hugging Face cache, shared with the recipes.

perf.source: a DGX Spark owner's llama-benchy run on the NVIDIA forum (NVFP4 with MTP drafts, served by a third-party engine, not this vLLM build): 35.9 tok/s alone, 80.9 across 4, prefill ≈3,176 tok/s. Spark Swapper measures the vLLM build after the first load

inkling.eta: several minutes the first time (CUDA-graph capture); a few minutes after
notes: Takes images as input (each side 40–4,096 px), sent as image_url parts in the OpenAI chat API; no audio. Video is not listed as an input.

Inkling support isn't in a vLLM release yet: this uses vLLM's own Inkling build (vllm/vllm-openai:inkling-2-mini, arm64, pinned to commit 7cb5dae) and the vLLM recipe's DGX Spark settings, which cap the 1M native context at 262,144.

Reasoning comes back in message.reasoning; the default effort is high. Send chat_template_kwargs {"reasoning_effort": "low"} (none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max) for shorter thinking. The model card warns it can get stuck in long reasoning loops, so replies are capped at 32,768 tokens unless the request sets max_tokens.
If the DSpark drafts fail to start on your box, remove the --speculative-config argument in a site override (models.json): about 35 tok/s is reported without them too.

ornith.title: Ornith 1.5 122B
ornith.tagline: A 125B mixture of experts at 4 bits per weight (EXL3): 65 GB of weights, 262K native context, within 0.014 nats of full precision.

install.time: 40–90 minutes: downloads 65.6 GB of weights and builds the ExLlamaV3 image (it compiles CUDA kernels)
install.note: Building needs about 24 GiB of free memory. If a large model is serving, switch to a smaller one first.

perf.source: not published (the model card says throughput wasn't measured) — Spark Swapper measures it after the first load

ornith.eta: a few minutes (loads ~64 GiB of weights)
notes: Experimental: the weights' card only reports a short text smoke test with ExLlamaV3 v1.6.1; vision, long context and speed are untested, and ExLlamaV3 on the Spark's GPU architecture is compiled here from source.
The first install builds the ExLlamaV3 + TabbyAPI image on the box: 20–40 minutes, about 24 GiB of free memory while it compiles.

vllmfp4.title: Qwen3.8 Flash Next (NVIDIA FP4 · vLLM)
vllmfp4.tagline: NVIDIA's own FP4 build of Flash Next on the community b12x vLLM image: the same checkpoint TensorFold serves, through vLLM's API.
vllmfp4.engine: vLLM · b12x kernels · NVIDIA FP4 (QAD) · MTP

install.time: 1–2 hours: pulls the ~10 GB vLLM image and downloads the ~96 GiB checkpoint (skipped if the TensorFold recipe already fetched it)
install.note: Needs about 110 GB of free disk when nothing is downloaded yet.

perf.source: not published (NVIDIA's card reports accuracy only) — Spark Swapper measures it after the first load

vllmfp4.eta: several minutes the first time (kernel compilation); faster after
notes: Uses the same checkpoint as the TensorFold recipe: if that is installed, nothing is downloaded again.
NVIDIA's card says the checkpoint needs community vLLM containers until the format lands upstream; this one is eugr/spark-vllm-b12x, pinned to the 2026-10-15 build.

standard.title: Qwen3.8 27B (SGLang)
standard.tagline: The dependable one: biggest context (1M with YaRN), steady tool use.

install.time: 10–20 minutes: pulls the SGLang image and downloads ~20 GB of weights

perf.source: the recipe's own benchmark (EAGLE/MTP, code probe; ~18 tok/s on long prose)

flash.title: Qwen3.8 Flash Next (vLLM)
flash.tagline: The original Flash Next recipe, with a longer window. Its authors now recommend the TensorFold version above.

install.time: 1–2 hours: downloads the ~99 GiB checkpoint; the first start builds a ~27 GiB table

perf.source: sparkDash sweep in the recipe's README (prose)

notes: The one way to serve Flash Next abliterated at 512K: the TensorFold card's 512K/1M build runs a different (INT4) checkpoint the abliteration overlay can't graft onto, and its 256K build has no YaRN. Turn on Abliterated in this card's Options….

contexts.label: 256K
contexts.detail: the model's native window — leaves room for pictures

contexts.label: 512K
contexts.detail: the longest chats (YaRN) — no room for pictures

switches.name: ablit
switches.label: Abliterated
switches.detail: drowzeys's Keys abliterated checkpoint (the same Mia NVFP4 weights with the refusal direction projected out), served by this recipe's ABLIT=1 — at 256K or 512K. A separate ~99 GiB gated download, on the first start only.
switches.warn: This model has had its safety refusals removed. The checkpoint is gated: accept its terms on Hugging Face (signed in) and save a token on the Settings tab first. The first start downloads ~99 GiB before it loads.
